description: Hand-maintained declarations for tools/parity/build_parity.mjs (docs/MAPLE_ISLAND_PARITY.md). categories.<id>.runtime and mechanics[].runtime declare the code an entry needs before it can be more than 'missing': every path or glob in files must exist and every contains marker must be found in a file matching its glob; partial names an older implementation that makes the entries 'partial' with its issue. A runtime declaration only says the code exists; evidence (parity-tagged checks) is what verifies an entry. mechanics[] are the Definition-of-Done rows that are not one canonical record each: category (default map-mechanics) places the row, accepts lists aliases (test keys that prove the same requirement; an alias may name no other entry and no other row's alias), real_game asks for a playtest check (true) or waives the category's need for one (false), source_gaps marks a documented source-data gap (the sources give no value). Keys of mechanics, cross_reference and canonical_verification are the parity keys tests tag (contract C6). canonical_verification[].requires names a state the shipped data must be in before the row can be more than partial ({"drops_schema_version": 2}: every drop record is schema v2, contract C1). playtest_tags gives parity keys to the hard checks of a scenario whose names match (scenario: report.json scenario name or names; match: a regular expression on the check name; keys: templates, $1..$9 are the match's groups; why: the review note). Every rule here was written against the check names of a real report and gives only keys the check proves; a rule that matches no check of its scenario's report is reported by the generator. out_of_scope maps a key to why Iteration Three leaves it out (content outside Maple Island, or a mechanic excluded as an isometric adaptation, said so in its text). adaptations name game/data/misostory files; "<file>.json#<key>" names one top-level section of the file, which must exist (a stale section fails the build). pending_source_reads maps a key to a value a source publishes on a page nobody has read yet ({read: the page, resolves: what it settles, decision, fields: for a record, the fields its gaps name; why}): such an entry is not a source-data gap, is never excused and stays partial (open for the exit criterion) until the read is done; a declaration the data no longer supports fails the build as stale. A drop record's excluded KuroDB candidate row makes its member pending even when undeclared (the generator warns).

mechanics.name: Fall damage: MeowDB documents a formula (a landing after at least 45 consecutive fast-falling movement updates deals base 24, rising to 36; maps can disable it); MisoStory applies none (adaptation)
mechanics.brief: Do Not Trust Existing Content Merely Because It Exists (a MeowDB mechanic the player meets)
source_gaps: The canonical rule cannot be applied as published: the length of one movement update, the unit of its N counter, is not documented (formulas/movement.json fall_damage.gaps), and MeowDB says 'Maps can disable fall damage' without naming the maps that do, so whether Maple Island's maps have fall damage is unknown. MisoStory applies no fall damage (presentation.json fall_recovery, verified: false): a MisoStory adaptation, not a canonical statement

out_of_scope.mechanic:crouch-down-jump: Excluded as an isometric adaptation (a MisoStory decision, verified: false): in MisoStory's isometric 3D maps the down key (move_down, S) walks toward the camera, so there is no crouch stance, and the terrain has no pass-through floors (the player stands on the highest walkable collision under its feet; no one-way platform layer exists), so a crouching jump has nothing to drop through. The player reaches a lower floor by walking off its edge (PLAYER_AND_CAMERA.md: the player drops once its centre is 0.15 m past an edge, as in classic) or by a rope or ladder. No input reaches the crouched (prone) attack that combat_formula.gd can resolve either. Listed for DEFERRED
